title: Protocol for tumor dissociation and fluorescence-activated cell sorting of human head and neck cancers
protocol: Pre-warm a 4.7 mL aliquot of RPMI or Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle Medium in a 15 mL conical tube using a 37°C incubator.
Thaw a frozen aliquot of enzyme H, R, and A on room temperature or on ice.
Add 200 μL Enzyme H to the pre-warmed medium.
Add 100 μL Enzyme R to the pre-warmed medium.
Add 25 μL enzyme A to the pre-warmed medium.
Mix all components in the 15 mL conical tube thoroughly.
Remove and discard fat, fibrous tissue, clots, and necrotic areas from the tumor sample on a dry petri dish at room temperature using two sterile scalpels.
Thoroughly mince the remaining tumor tissue into approximately 1–2 mm pieces.
Transfer tumor sample to a sterile petri dish after removing fatty, fibrous, hemorrhagic, and necrotic areas.
Mince tumor tissue into 1–2 mm pieces using two sterile scalpels.
Transfer minced tumor sample to a 15 mL conical tube as much as possible using a scalpel.
Add 10 mL PBS to the petri dish and pipette it over the surface multiple times to collect residual tissue fragments.
Transfer PBS solution containing residual tissue fragments to the 15 mL conical tube with the minced tumor sample.
Centrifuge the 15 mL conical tube at 300 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate and discard the supernatant from the centrifuged sample.
Add pre-warmed enzyme mix to the pellet.
Triturate (pipette up and down approximately 20 times) with a 10 mL serological pipette.
If the specimen is larger than 2 g or 1 cm3, triturate the sample using a 25 mL pipette in a 50 mL conical tube.
Titrate technique based on ease of aspirating tissue fragments into the pipette.
Stop triturating and proceed to incubation if difficulty occurs during pipetting.
Incubate the sample in a water or bead bath at 37°C for 10 min, inverting the tube every few minutes.
Switch to triturating with a 5 mL serological pipette when possible.
Triturate the sample in contact with the bottom of the conical tube, avoiding buildup of negative or positive pressure in the pipette.
Monitor the media for cloudiness as an indication of cell dissociation.
Remove 90 μL sample into a 1.7 mL microcentrifuge tube and add 10 μL trypan blue.
Assess individual cells under the microscope; repeat trituration if most cells are clustered together.
Pipette the single cell suspension through a 100 μm strainer into a 50 mL conical tube.
Filtration of single cell suspension using a 100 μm strainer.
Pipette the sample onto the bottom of the strainer, not the sides, to avoid loss during removal.
Wash the strainer with 10 mL media (RPMI 1640 or DMEM) and then wash cells by pipetting up and down.
Store cell strainer containing residual tissue on ice or at room temperature for reprocessing if needed.
Centrifuge the sample for 5 min at 300 g at 4°C.
Aspirate and discard supernatant, removing last 1 mL carefully with a P1000 pipette to avoid disrupting pellet.
If necessary, remove red blood cells using RBC lysis solution if pellet appears red.
Proceed to step 19 if pellet appears white.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL Hanks’ Balanced Salt Solution (HBSS).
Prepare 1× RBC lysis solution by mixing 1 mL RBC solution with 9 mL ddH2O.
Add 9 mL of 1× RBC lysis solution to 1 mL cell suspension in HBSS.
Vortex for 5 seconds.
Incubate the mixture for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Centrifuge the sample for 5 minutes at 300 g and 4°C.
Aspirate and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend cells in PBS + 1% BSA to a final volume of 100 μL after adding antibodies.
Add 10 μL CD45-VioBlue, 5 μL CD90-PE, and 5 μL CD31-PE-Cy7 antibodies to the cell suspension.
Incubate the sample on ice covered with foil for 20 minutes.
Centrifuge the sample for 5 min at 300 g at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant.
Wash cells with 1 mL PBS, 1% BSA.
Centrifuge the sample for 5 min at 300 g at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant.
Re-suspend the cells in 0.5–1.5 mL PBS, 1% BSA (volume correlating with pellet size).
Transfer the re-suspended cells to a FACS tube with a 35 μm filter top.
Pipette carefully through the filter.
Change the top of the FACS tube to a non-filtered top.
Keep the samples on ice protected from light by covering with foil.
Add calcein AM (1:1000) to stain live cells and To-Pro-3 iodide (1:3000) to stain dead cells immediately prior to sorting.
Gently vortex the sample for 1 min to allow staining.
Sort as appropriate for subsequent applications.
For plate-based single-cell RNA-sequencing protocols, sort 1 cell per well of a 96-well plate prepared with 10 μL lysis buffer (buffer TCL + 1% beta-mercaptoethanol).
For droplet-based single-cell RNA-sequencing protocols, sort cells into a 1.7 mL Lobind Eppendorf microcentrifuge tube containing PBS with 1% BSA.
Sort cells directly into serum-containing media in a 1.7 mL microcentrifuge tube for cell and 3D organoid culture applications.
Use a FACSAria Fusion Special Order System or equivalent for FACS.
Employ 488 nm, 640 nm, 405 nm, and 561 nm lasers during sorting.
Utilize a 100 μm nozzle for cell sorting.
